gonioscopy causes short-term reversible steepening of central corneal curvature as measured by Simulated Keratometer.
the act of gonio-scopy causes a reversible steepening of the cornea, which can be measured with topographic methods.
the effect of Gonioscopes on corneal surface curvature is short lived and is not clinically significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a very specific issue in ophthalmology, namely the short-term effect on corneal measurements following gonioscopy.
the effect of the act of gonio-scopy on corneol surface measurements and the effect of the type of gonioscope used.
the effect of gonioscopic contact lens on the central corneoscleral curvature and corneal curvature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Gonioscopy with Goldmann or Sussen contact lens does not affect the accuracy of corneal curvature measurement with the auto-keratometer, but it does affect the accuracy of the topographic measurement.

the use of topography based Sim K to calculate intraocular lens power after gonioscopy may lead to an overestimation of the power of the lens implant, which may result in a post-operative refractive error that is hyperopic.
gonioscopy causes a transient change in corneal topographic curvature, which is not present with Auto-K readings and is not clinically relevant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Gonioscopic measurements can affect the cornea and that these changes are reversible.
Gonioscopy does not appear to affect keratometry readings as measured by the Auto-K.
the effect of gonioscopic procedures on corneal topographic measurements is transient and can be ignored after a minimum of 15 minutes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of the act of goniscopy is transient and reversible.
the effect of gonioscope contact on topographically derived Sim-K is transient and that the effect on IOL calculation is minimal.
